title: Career roadmap · Wellness Director
summary: Build toward senior wellness leadership by combining yoga and naturopathy expertise with programme design, preventive-health research, operations, people management, evaluation and organisational strategy.

facts.Current degree: Ph.D. - Physical Education, Sports Science & Yoga
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes the Ph.D. begins in 2026 and the target is a senior role leading wellness programmes, centres, institutes, corporate wellbeing functions, health-promotion programmes or integrated wellness organisations. Clinical practice should only be undertaken within the scope of the professional qualification and applicable regulations.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build evidence-based wellness expertise, complete the Ph.D., develop programmes and gain experience measuring participant outcomes.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Move into programme or centre management and specialise in corporate wellness, preventive health, yoga therapy research, lifestyle programmes or wellness operations.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead multidisciplinary teams, budgets, partnerships and multi-site wellness programmes with measurable outcomes.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Lead a major wellness organisation or portfolio while integrating evidence, technology, prevention, workforce wellbeing and responsible business practices.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Wellness Researcher/Programme Coordinator
2030–2035: Wellness Programme Manager → Wellness Centre Manager
2035–2040: Senior Wellness Manager → Regional/Portfolio Wellness Director
2040–2046: Wellness Director → National Wellness Programme Director / Chief Wellness Officer
Ph.D. research routes

At senior level, the role should be about measurable wellbeing outcomes and organisational performance, not simply offering more wellness activities. Build systems for programme quality, participant safety, outcome measurement, staff development, financial sustainability and evidence review. A strong Wellness Director should also be able to distinguish scientifically supported interventions from unsupported health claims and maintain clear boundaries between wellness services and regulated clinical care.
